newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Biplane explodes in Russian north, at least 13 dead.
newsitem.headline: Biplane explodes in Russian north, at least 13 dead.

text.p: An antiquated Antonov An-2 biplane exploded shortly after take-off in northern Russia on Thursday, killing all 13 or 14 people on board, a local Emergencies Ministry official said.
Investigators were still on their way to the crash site, at the village of Bolshaya Pyssa some 200 km (120 miles) south of the Arctic Circle in the semi-autonomous Komi region.

The official, speaking from the regional capital Syktyvkar, told Reuters the co-pilot of the single-engined aircraft was thrown clear but died later in hospital. The pilot and all 11 or 12 passengers were killed immediately.
It was not clear whether a teenage boy was among the dead or whether he had left the doomed commuter plane on its final stop.

Aircraft are a vital means of transport in the vast and barren wastes of Russia's Far North. But safety standards in the economically depressed former Soviet Union have been severely criticised in recent years.
Those problems were spotlighted this week after a Kazakh cargo plane was involved in the world's worst mid-air collision over India on Tuesday. Some 350 people were killed.
